Local Synapse Snapshots

Source: vignettes/synapse-snapshots.Rmd
synapse-snapshots.Rmd

A local synapse snapshot is a copy of the whole CRANTb synapse table on your own machine. Partner queries for hundreds of neurons then take seconds rather than minutes, at a materialisation version or right up to the current time. You also get the full synapse table, including the position of every synapse.

The code is shared with the aedes package, which must be installed (it is only suggested by crantr):

pak::pak("flyconnectome/aedes")

See the aedes Local Synapse Snapshots article for how snapshots work, how recent edits are handled and how they are built and published. Everything there applies to crantr, with aedes_* functions replaced by their crant_* equivalents.

Getting started

You need access to the CRANT CAVE datastack.

library(crantr)
crant_use_snapshot()

The first time, crant_use_snapshot() offers to download a snapshot; you can also do this with crant_download_snapshot(). This is about 1.8 GB, once only: 1.35 GB of static data for the 88 million synapses (ids, supervoxels, positions and size), which never changes, and a 0.4 GB base snapshot giving the root ids of every synapse at one materialisation version. After that, daily checkpoints of a few tens of KB are fetched automatically when you use the snapshot.

Partner queries

Once a snapshot is selected, crant_partner_summary() and crant_partners() answer queries from it whenever they can, and otherwise fall back to CAVE. Use method = "local" to insist on the snapshot, or method = "cave" to skip it.

id <- "576460752684030043"
# up to the second: edits since the newest snapshot are fetched from CAVE
crant_partner_summary(id, partners = "inputs")
# at a materialisation version, with no CAVE lookups
crant_partner_summary(id, partners = "inputs", version = crant_version())
# individual synapses, with their positions
crant_partners(id, partners = "output", method = "local")

Root ids only make sense at one time, so for an analysis that makes several queries fix the time once and use it throughout:

now <- Sys.time()
ins <- crant_partner_summary(id, partners = "inputs", timestamp = now)
outs <- crant_partner_summary(id, partners = "outputs", timestamp = now)

The synapse table

crant_synapse_data() gives the whole table as a lazy dplyr table backed by DuckDB, so you can run your own queries over all synapses, at a snapshot or (with timestamp) any later time. details = TRUE adds supervoxels, positions (in nm) and size.

library(dplyr)
id64 <- bit64::as.integer64(id)
crant_synapse_data(timestamp = now) |>
  filter(pre_root %in% id64) |>
  count(post_root, sort = TRUE) |>
  collect()

Updating a snapshot

Snapshots are updated automatically, but you can save your own snapshot at a later time, which makes repeated queries at that time fast:

crant_update_snapshot()
